key_insight: Independent benchmarking shows that specialized open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation models can outperform newer general-purpose and foundation approaches, but performance varies widely by dataset and pathology.
clinical_relevance: Accurate muscle segmentation supports MRI-based biomarkers such as volumetry, radiomics, and fat fraction quantification, so errors can materially affect research and clinical interpretation in neuromuscular disease.
method: Compared 8 open-source segmentation tools; 6 ran independently and 2 required prior muscle labeling.
Evaluated 3D MRI volumes from three base datasets and additional derived datasets.
Assessed both quantitative performance and qualitative usability across methods.
evidence_signal: The benchmark found substantial performance variation across methods and datasets, with many tools performing worse on pathological cases and domain-specific models generally outperforming foundation or general-purpose architectures.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or rare pathologies, and some high-performing tools may still be harder to deploy in practice.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
